name: Dominic Varghese
label: Computational Materials Science Ph.D. Candidate
summary: I combine first-principles simulations, physics-informed machine learning, and high-performance computing to understand materials and accelerate their discovery. My research connects oxide interfaces, lattice dynamics, and machine-learning interatomic potentials.

work_experience.summary: Modeling the flexoelectric effect in oxides with Prof. Turan Birol.
highlights: Build DFT datasets with VASP and ABINIT, fine-tune equivariant GNN interatomic potentials (MACE, NequIP, PET), and run simulations on GPU-accelerated HPC clusters.
Study how epitaxial strain enhances flexoelectric response through optical phonon softening using DFPT, Landau theory, and group theory.

work_experience.summary: Predicting lattice dynamics with Prof. Turan Birol.
highlights: Predict high-dimensional dynamical matrices from nearest-neighbor force-constant features to infer phonon dispersions under strain and pressure.
Validate predictions against neutron-scattering experiments and capture strain-induced acoustic branch softening.

work_experience.summary: Research on the non-linear Hall effect in Ferroelectrics under the guidance of Prof. Awadhesh Narayan.
highlights: Identified optimal doping concentrations in ferroelectric perovskites that maximize the Berry Curvature Dipole (BCD), leading to an enhancement of the Non-Linear Hall effect.
Systematically varied doping concentrations and computed BCD using Quantum Espresso and Wannier90, successfully demonstrating a tunable electronic response.

projects.title: Polymer property prediction
projects.summary: From repeat-unit SMILES to five polymer properties: a chemistry-aware pipeline combining molecular graphs with physics-informed residual learning.
highlights: Benchmarks GraphGPS, PNA, GATv2, and GINE with cluster-based cross-validation.
Repository-reported five-fold OOF weighted MAE: 0.05154 for the physics-cascade hybrid.

projects.title: Crystal Symmetry Lab
projects.summary: A browser-based 3D workbench for exploring crystal symmetry, strain-induced symmetry breaking, and physical-property tensors.
highlights: Visualizes space-group operations and atomic site symmetries from CIF and VASP structure files.
Connects strain and order parameters to subgroup changes and symmetry-allowed tensors.

projects.title: WARDEN · AI co-scientist
projects.summary: An in-silico workflow for atomic layer deposition research, combining agent-guided screening with deterministic physics checks.
highlights: Includes bounded feedback loops, evidence acquisition, persistent records, and reaction-kinetics workflows.
Research prototype: the offline demo is synthetic; live services and MACE scientific performance remain unverified in the repository.

projects.title: Piezoelectric Modulus Prediction Using Machine Learning
projects.summary: Developed a complete machine learning pipeline to classify and predict the piezoelectric modulus for a large set of inorganic materials from the JARVIS database.
highlights: Trained on 1,354 inorganic materials from JARVIS; reached 78% classification accuracy.
Used crystal symmetry features and transfer learning to achieve a regression RMSE of 0.49.
